1.mascotDialogue: All the splitting is only bookkeeping — the true sorting work happens entirely within the merge step, comparing two already-sorted halves and interleaving them correctly.

2.mascotDialogue: Lines 9 and 10 are the merge's heart — compare the fronts of both halves, take the smaller, advance only that side. Lines 12 and 13 gather whichever half still holds leftovers, once the other empties.

3.mascotDialogue: Notice this view shows no swaps at all — merge sort does not swap elements in place. It writes the smaller of two fronts into a fresh position, with every comparison.

4.mascotDialogue: It is easy to believe the merge is finished the moment the main comparison loop ends — but one side almost always finishes before the other, and forgetting to drain the leftovers loses real data, silently.
